reason: V16 is the first prompt-only Brachiosaurus candidate in this route to combine the high shoulder, taller forelimbs, rising neck, four visible pillar feet, and a visibly short thick tapering tail. V4 remains a useful i2i comparison, but v16 better solves the repeated diplodocid whip-tail failure. V15 and v17 stay as review holds because their body plans are useful, but their tails read longer or less compact than v16.
rejectIfPromoting: tail becomes a long thin diplodocid whip or is cropped
forelimbs and hind limbs become equal height or shoulder drops near hip line
neck becomes low and horizontal like Apatosaurus/Diplodocus
feet are hidden, fused, hoof-like, or unclear enough to block four-leg review
head becomes crocodile-like, toothed, predator-like, or too large
